paragraphs: The core of the work of agricultural and food scientists is turning animal, food, crop or soil problems into testable experiments and data-based conclusions, and taking responsibility for where those conclusions can be used. When judging fit, first look at whether you are willing to give time to sampling frames, controls, replicates, raw records and failed experiments, and only then consider interests.

Three small self-test tasks: rewrite 'does a certain feed additive increase milk yield' as an experiment with a control, replicates and metrics; use one public dataset to complete cleaning, a baseline and an error statement; and explain the uncertainty of a conclusion to a non-research colleague. Doing them incompletely is normal; the point is to observe your own real reaction to verifying detail, admitting what is unknown, and going back to the field to check. (Editorial suggestion, not a hiring standard.)

People more likely to adapt: those willing to work with samples, data and field conditions over the long term, able to accept failed experiments and keep the failure record, and not averse to the idea that 'a conclusion only extends to certain conditions'. If you want only conceptual discussion and a good-looking result every time, the gap in experience is usually larger.

The U.S. wages and employment on this page use the BLS national combined occupation group basis (wages for 2025, month 5 (May); projection 2025—2035), and do not cover the self-employed or some agricultural workers; mainland China has no precise national wage distribution for this occupation, so industry-sector figures serve only as a broad reference and cannot be treated as an individual's starting pay or median.

In one sentence: a role that uses life science and statistical methods to turn specific 'farm to table' problems into reviewable conclusions; precision, field constraints and responsibility for results all have to be accepted together.

The tasks of agricultural and food scientists fall into three categories: designing and running experiments (question, hypothesis, control, sampling, analysis); turning results into executable plans (process, quality standards, technical reports and recommendations); and recording and collaboration (raw data, versions, review and cross-team communication). The weight of the three varies with the animal, food, soil and plant directions.

O*NET 19-1011.00 (animal scientists): study the genetics, nutrition, reproduction, growth and development of farm animals; tasks include researching feed nutritive value and feeding, breeding and disease-control methods, and writing up results for the scientific community and producers. This profile is a single-occupation basis and is not the combined basis of the three directions on this page.

Food Safety Law of the People's Republic of China (amended in 2025, Presidential Order No. 81): food producers and traders are responsible for the safety of the food they produce and trade; food safety work follows prevention first, risk management, whole-process control and social co-governance. The BLS combined occupation group 19-1010 contains three directions: animal scientists 19-1011, food scientists and technologists 19-1012, and soil and plant scientists 19-1013; they study the efficiency, quality and safety of agricultural and food production. Scientists focus on research design and interpretation, technicians may also analyse results and prepare reports; agricultural engineers focus on equipment, facilities and engineering systems, and each position's authority must be checked separately.

Research design and field or production-line sampling positions
Samples cover only a few batches, locations or varieties but are written up as a general rule, which can mislead farmers or production decisions.

A batch of samples had no temperature recorded during transport and the test results deviate markedly from historical levels, yet a report was still demanded directly.

values: Practice material (fictional case)

Task statement: a fictional greenhouse uses 6 independent trial pots of the same batch and variety of seedlings, randomly assigned to two nutrient regimes A/B with 3 pots per group and all other growing conditions identical; after 14 days the above-ground fresh weight of each pot is measured in grams, with no missing values.
Group and measurement record: group A 10, 12 and 11 grams; group B 13, 14 and 15 grams. The material is for paper analysis only and is not actual cultivation or fertilisation advice.

The task statement provides no price, yield, significance or approval information; it must not be added by the candidate, and no population, causal or commercial-promotion conclusion may be inferred from it.
Practice task
List the groups and the measurement record for each pot, calculate the means of groups A and B and the absolute and relative difference of B against A, keeping the working and the units.
Write a conclusion with its limitations, and state what further evidence is needed before generalising; the conclusion must give the scope of this observation and the sources of uncertainty.
Approach and reference

First check against the A/B grouping that the 6 measured values have no missing entries, then calculate step by step: mean A 11 grams, mean B 14 grams, difference 3 grams, relative difference 3/11 ≈ 27.3% (keeping the working and the units).

The conclusion describes only this observation of these 6 pots, and does not establish population significance, adequately proven causation or effective commercial promotion; the small sample, the single batch and site, and measurement error still limit the conclusion.

The portfolio only demonstrates the level of analytical preparation; it does not constitute actual cultivation or fertilisation advice, a skills test or a hiring test, and does not represent any qualification or authorisation; the open part may propose different reasonable follow-up verification plans (such as replicates across more batches and sites, or a pre-registered analysis plan), but must not add price, yield, significance or approval information that the task statement does not contain.

paragraphs: Qualifications for this occupation fall into two categories: education and training reflect systematic ability and are usually evidenced by institutional coursework and on-the-job accumulation; where inspection and testing, food safety management or release are involved, whether additional qualification or authorisation is required follows the regulations in force in mainland China and the competent authority's rules, and U.S. material must not be used as a basis for authorisation.

Research conclusions are the responsibility of the researchers who designed and signed them; release, recall and regulatory handling are decided by authorised positions under local regulations. Holding the data does not automatically confer approval authority (Food Safety Law of the People's Republic of China, amended in 2025).

On the U.S. side, the O*NET 19-1011.00 education survey (43% doctorate, 22% master's, 13% bachelor's, respondent shares) and the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook are used to explain industry practice and the education basis, and do not constitute a qualification basis in mainland China.

Those intending to enter should check the education, coursework, experimental and safety training and qualification requirements in official information, and apply and train through official channels; this page does not constitute legal advice.

items.title: Notes on qualification and authorisation boundaries

paragraphs: Sample applicability: this page does not cite any recruitment posting as evidence of wages or demand; recruitment conditions, education and qualification requirements vary by region and organisation, and the official publications of the competent authority and the employer prevail. This page also does not provide a by-city wage distribution or hiring pass rate for this occupation: the U.S. side gives BLS and O*NET agricultural and food scientists wages, employment and projections, and the mainland China side gives a broad industry-sector reference and the institutional framework; the two are not the same statistical basis.

To judge whether a position belongs to this occupation, look at the task description rather than the title: whether it involves experimental design and hypotheses, sampling and testing, statistical analysis and verification, turning conclusions into plans or standards, and data and record management.

entries.question: What do agricultural and food scientists do every day?

entries.answer: This occupation is responsible for research design and interpretation of conclusions; technicians carry out sampling and testing; agricultural engineers are responsible for equipment, facilities and engineering systems; data scientists provide general methods but do not automatically take responsibility for agricultural experiments or food release.
